title: Engine Driven Pump — Removal

issue.reason: Original issue of the engine driven pump removal task.

abstract: Removal of an engine driven pump from the accessory gearbox, including the pressure decay check and the case drain sample that have to be taken before the line is broken, and the drive spline condition record.

sections.purpose: This task gives the removal of one engine driven pump from the accessory gearbox, together with the case drain fluid sample and the drive spline examination.
sections.job_setup_note: The hydraulic system must be depressurised and the reservoir must be at the servicing level or below. The fan cowl doors must be open and on their stays. The case drain sample has to be taken before the line is broken, because it is the only way to see the wear debris signature that the shop uses. Spillage protection must be in place under the pylon.
sections.procedure: 1. WARNING: MAKE SURE THAT THE HYDRAULIC SYSTEM IS DEPRESSURISED AND THAT THE RESERVOIR IS NOT PRESSURISED BEFORE ANY CONNECTION IS BROKEN. 2. Open the fan cowl doors and put them on their stays. 3. Remove the pylon lower access panel. 4. Before anything is disconnected, do the pressure decay check: run the system to the check pressure, shut the pump down and record the fall over sixty seconds at the case drain sampling point. A slow decay with a normal case drain flow points at a worn pump; a fast decay with a low case drain flow points at a starved inlet and the pump is usually serviceable. 5. Take the case drain fluid sample at the sampling point and identify it with the aircraft registration and the pump serial number. 6. Close the pump isolation valve D2910110251872 and confirm the position indicator. 7. CAUTION: SUPPORT THE RETURN PIPE WHILE THE UNION IS SLACKENED. A LOADED PIPE SPRINGS WHEN THE UNION RELEASES. 8. Disconnect and cap the return pipe D2910004303006 and the pressure line. 9. Release the clamp 280GG8 and move the harness clear. 10. Remove the pump retaining nuts and withdraw the pump squarely from the gearbox pad. 11. Examine the drive spline for wear, for fretting and for missing lubricant, and record what is found. 12. Fit the gearbox pad blank and the pump transit caps. 13. Recover the spilled fluid and account for the anchor nuts AES818405K5 against the joint diagram.
sections.close_out: Make sure that the gearbox pad is blanked and that every hydraulic connection is capped. Send the case drain sample to the laboratory with the pump serial number and the running hours. Record the drive spline condition, the pump serial number and the removal reason in the aircraft technical record.

safety_precautions: Depressurise the hydraulic system and confirm the reservoir is not pressurised.
Put the fan cowl doors on their stays.
Put the hydraulic spillage protection in position.

title: Engine Driven Pump — Removal

issue.reason: Note added that the pressure decay check in this task is also the acceptance test of the centre tank screen installation and may not be altered in isolation.

abstract: Removal of an engine driven pump from the accessory gearbox, including the pressure decay check that the fuel screen installation also uses as its acceptance test, the case drain sample and the drive spline condition record.

sections.purpose: This task gives the removal of one engine driven pump from the accessory gearbox, together with the case drain fluid sample and the drive spline examination.
sections.job_setup_note: The hydraulic system must be depressurised and the reservoir must be at the servicing level or below. The fan cowl doors must be open and on their stays. The pressure decay check at step 4 and the case drain sample at step 5 both have to be taken before any line is broken, because they are the only way to see the wear debris signature and the inlet behaviour that the shop uses. The decay figures and the sixty second window in this task are also quoted as the acceptance test of the centre tank boost pump installation, where they discriminate a starved inlet from a worn pump on a fuel screen change; neither figure may be altered here without the fuel task being re-issued with it. Spillage protection must be in place under the pylon.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. On aircraft at the anti-cavitation relief valve standard the relief valve stays with the aircraft and is not removed with the pump. The pressure decay check figures are shared with the centre tank boost pump installation task and are maintained together with it.
